samples.text:
The bar chart give information about how many international tourists came to one country from 2014 to 2024, and the pie chart shows the reasons why they visited in 2024.

Firstly, looking at the bar chart, the number of tourists was 8.2 million in 2014 and it increased to 9.5 million in 2016. Then it rose again to 11.1 million in 2018. However, in 2020 there was a big drop and the number fell to only 3.4 million, which is the lowest in the period. After that, the tourists increased again to 7.8 million in 2022 and reached to 12.6 million in 2024, that was the highest number.

Also, the pie chart shows that holiday was the main purpose of visit with 54%, which is more than a half. Visiting family and friends was 19% and business was 15%. The study had 8% and the smallest purpose was medical with only 4%.

Overall, the number of tourists went up in the period apart from a sharp fall in 2020, and most of visitors came for holiday.
samples.why: Overview present but basic and placed at the end · key figures accurate but reported mechanically · repetitive linking (Firstly, Then, Also) · adequate vocabulary · several article, preposition and agreement errors.

samples.text:
The bar chart illustrates changes in the number of overseas visitors to a particular country over a ten-year period from 2014, while the pie chart breaks down their reasons for travelling there in 2024.

Overall, tourist arrivals grew steadily apart from a dramatic collapse in 2020, after which they recovered strongly to reach a peak in the final year. As for the purpose of visits, holidays accounted for the majority, whereas medical trips were the least common.

In 2014, 8.2 million international tourists arrived in the country, and this figure climbed gradually to 9.5 million in 2016 and 11.1 million in 2018. In 2020, however, arrivals plummeted to just 3.4 million, less than one third of previous total. The number then rebounded to 7.8 million in 2022 before hitting 12.6 million in 2024, the highest point in the period.

Turning to the pie chart, more than half of visitors (54%) came for a holiday. Visiting family or friends was the second most common reason, at 19%, followed closely by business at 15%. Only a small proportion of tourists travelled for study or medical purpose, with 8% and 4% respectively.
samples.why: Clear overview of trend and main purpose · key features well highlighted with a useful comparison · logical progression and good range of linkers · some less common vocabulary · two minor slips.

samples.text:
The two charts provide information about international tourism in one country: the bar chart tracks annual arrivals between 2014 and 2024, and the pie chart shows why visitors came in the final year.

Arrivals followed a broadly upward trajectory over the decade, interrupted only by a sharp slump in 2020 from which the sector had more than recovered by 2024. Leisure was by far the dominant motive for travel, accounting for over half of all visits.

In 2014 the country received 8.2 million foreign visitors, a figure that rose steadily to 11.1 million by 2018. This growth was abruptly reversed in 2020, when arrivals collapsed to 3.4 million, roughly 30% of the 2018 level. A strong recovery followed, with numbers more than doubling to 7.8 million in 2022 and then climbing to a ten-year high of 12.6 million in 2024, some 1.5 million above the pre-2020 peak.

Regarding the purpose of visits, holidaymakers made up 54% of tourists in 2024, almost three times the proportion who came to see family or friends (19%). Business travel accounted for a similar share, at 15%, while study and medical treatment were comparatively minor reasons, representing just 8% and 4% respectively.
samples.why: Well-placed overview linking both charts · figures selected skilfully with accurate derived comparisons · seamless cohesion · precise vocabulary (trajectory, slump, recovery) · wide range of structures, error-free.
